phase: G — judged. Four rounds in, the line is flat.
state: Four rounds of critics: 4.1, 4.1, 3.9, 3.6 on the critic mean — but those are four DIFFERENT critics and the numbers are not strictly comparable. The blind side-by-side is the comparable measure, same ten dimensions and same opponents every time: 1-1-8, then 0-2-8, then 0-2-8, now 1-2-7. Essentially flat, slightly better. Information design won outright again this round.

verdict.summary: Critic 3.6/10 — first impression 4, world 3, legibility 4, automation 2, heat 7, night 2, onboarding 4, feel 4, coherence 3, keep-playing 3. Blind: OURS 1 (information design), EVEN 2 (pressure and consequence, onboarding), THEIRS 7. Heat and survival has held at 6-7 for four rounds and is the only pillar that has never wobbled.
verdict.biggest_gap: Two gaps, and the second is a method failure. THE CRITIC: the automation pillar is OPTIONAL — logi_haul.gd HAUL_RANGE=96 covers the whole city and porters scale with population, so 19 porters move 19578 items while the belts move 2592. Belts carry 12% of goods and a player who never opens the Logistics tab loses nothing, in a game that invokes Factorio. THE BLIND JUDGE: the night still has no picture. It scanned the assault frame for the exact foe rim colour and found 105 pixels in two clusters — both were temperature labels. Ten hostiles alive, 21 agents drawn, zero findable. The builder that fixed contrast this round measured 11 of 11 enemies at deltaL 0.42 in its OWN test rig; in the shipped frame the under-attack red wash sits on top of the only cue that separates a foe from a citizen.
